Hi Maria — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Yes — we support AWS, Azure and GCP marketplace listings. Each has slightly different activation and invoicing flows.
- Direct PO: customers can either buy directly (we invoice) or purchase via the marketplace (cloud vendor invoices the buyer and remits to Redwood). For direct POs we require a W-9 (US) or equivalent tax documentation and a signed reseller/vendor agreement.
- Required vendor paperwork: vendor intake form, W-9 (or W8-BEN for international), SOW or listing description, bank remittance info, and company registration docs for marketplaces that require vendor verification.

I've attached our vendor intake template to this email — it lists the exact fields we need for all three marketplaces (pricing matrix, SKU mapping, tax id, PO routing preferences). Fill that out and return with your W9 and SOW and we'll open the intake ticket.

Hi Maria — thanks for sending the docs and for the call earlier. Quick summary and next steps so everything is clear for procurement and legal on your side: 

1) Marketplace vs direct PO
- AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace: easiest for buyers. Marketplace invoices are handled by the cloud vendor; buyers use marketplace subscriptions and Redwood receives remittance.
- Direct PO: we can accept direct POs. For those, buyers must route the PO to Redwood (billing@redwood.ai). If a buyer wants the PO to reference Skylab as the payee, we need the buyer to include the following language on the PO: 
  "Payment obligation to Redwood Inference. Skylab Systems is the service provider. Invoice to be issued by Redwood Inference, Inc., tax id XX-XXXXXXX."
  That allows us to reconcile vendor attribution to Skylab while ensuring payments flow to Redwood.

2) Paperwork checklist (what we still need from Skylab)
- Completed vendor-intake-form.xlsx (you said you'll return this tomorrow)
- Signed vendor agreement (we can send a DocuSign link once intake is accepted) — optional at intake stage but required pre-go-live
- Bank remittance details for marketplace payouts (if you want to receive direct payouts on any cloud platform)

3) Timelines
- AWS listing approval after we open the intake ticket: typical 3–6 weeks if all fields and docs are complete. Faster if you opt to go via AWS ISV private offers for pilots.

4) Next actions (owner)
- Maria: return filled vendor-intake-form.xlsx + any additional tax forms if non-US entities (due 2026-10-06).
